$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §2 (identity), §8 (fail closed), §9 (no confidence); docs/03-V0-SCOPE.md §1 items 1–5. Written from crates/ethos-parser-pdf/src/classify.rs; if the two disagree, the Rust is the implementation and 01-CONTRACT.md is the contract.
title: Classification artifact (DRAFT)
description: What a classifier observed, never what it concluded. Counts and named reason codes on two orthogonal axes, plus a derived boolean. There is no confidence field, no verdict, and no quality summary — the engine owns the observation, the caller owns the routing policy.

identity.description: artifact_type is `ethos.parser.classification.v0`; schema_version is `0.1.0`. Both DRAFT.

page_count.description: Total pages in the document. Deliberately NOT the driver of cost.

pages_sampled.description: min(page_count, profile.classify_sample_pages, profile.page_budget). The budget is in the minimum deliberately, so this field keeps meaning 'the pages this run intended to read' and stays equal to pages_content_scanned.

pages_content_scanned.$comment: The bound, made observable. Must equal pages_sampled. pdf-inspector advertises Sample(8) and then re-scans every page in a later phase, so asking for one page costs the same as asking for all of them (memo §16.3: Pages(1)=439ms, Sample(8)=412ms, Full=434ms on the same 492-page file). Measured here: 492 pages, 8 scanned, and classify time is flat — 246x the pages for 1.7x the time. A regression that reintroduced a full rescan would move this number and fail a test rather than surface as a benchmark surprise.

pages_with_text.description: Sampled pages carrying at least one text-showing operator.

ocr_reasons.description: Union of per-page OCR-need reasons, sorted and deduplicated. An OBSERVATION, never a routing decision.

layout_reasons.description: Union of per-page layout-hard reasons, sorted and deduplicated. None of these implies OCR — that independence is the point of the split and is asserted by a test.

needs_attention.$comment: DERIVED: !ocr_reasons.is_empty() || !layout_reasons.is_empty(). The lists are the truth; removing this field loses no information, which a property test asserts. Taken from LiteParse (parity checklist L3), where the same relationship holds.

pages.description: One row per SCANNED page, in page order. Not every page: bounded sampling means a large document has rows for the first N only, and what happened to the rest is assurance.page_states.

assurance.$comment: The L1 gate (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §7). ABSORBS M2's `not_detected` list, which no longer exists on the wire: the reason codes this profile never emits are now profile-scope limitations `garbled-reason-not-detected` and `multi-column-reason-not-detected`, carrying the same reasons verbatim. One vocabulary, one shape, one place to look. Note that a bounded classification is normally terminal_state `partial`: pages past the sample bound are `not_attempted`, which is not the same as observed and empty.

ocr_need_reason.title: OCR-need axis
ocr_need_reason.$comment: `sparse-text` requires short text ALONGSIDE imagery. Short text on its own is a short page, not a sparse one — LiteParse uses text_length < 20 unconditionally and compounds it with a vowel-frequency garble heuristic that strips items from the tally first, so an acronym-dense page (a NIST control table of AC-2/SC-7) can be reported as no-text when its text extracted perfectly (memo §18.3). Neither the vowel heuristic nor the unconditional length test exists here. `garbled` is never emitted by this profile. This said — see not_detected until v2-S14.1, which sent a reader to a list M4 absorbed and this schema's own `assurance` comment says no longer exists on the wire; the reason it names is carried by the profile-scope limitation `garbled-reason-not-detected` in `assurance.limitations`.

layout_complexity_reason.title: Layout-hard axis
layout_complexity_reason.$comment: Orthogonal to the OCR-need axis: none of these implies OCR. A dense financial table in crisp born-digital text needs no OCR at all. `multi-column` is never emitted by this profile — v0 has no stable rule, and pdf-inspector's flips on a single line of text (min_lines < 15), so a one-line edit reorders a whole page. This said See not_detected until v2-S14.1, for the same reason and with the same repair: the reason is carried by the profile-scope limitation `multi-column-reason-not-detected` in `assurance.limitations`.

index.$comment: 1-based, as the document numbers its own pages. pdf-inspector carries a 0-vs-1 inconsistency between two of its own result types; one indexing origin, established at the boundary, is how that is avoided.

text_bytes.$comment: Raw string-operand bytes inside text-showing operators, BEFORE any encoding or CMap decoding (which is M3). An estimate of extent, not a character count: a CID font may use two bytes per glyph, so this over-counts for CJK. Used only for presence and sparseness signals, never presented as a character count.

text_operators.$comment: Count of Tj, TJ, ' and " — all four. pdf-inspector omits " from its operator match, which loses text silently (parity checklist P6); at this layer the same omission would surface as a false no-text.
